mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the subject’s scope, naming the major questions, and previewing both conceptual explanation and practical application.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of a complex educational piece to establish relevance and give listeners a map of what will follow.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce an exhaustive list of subtopics without grouping them into a clear progression.

mechanics.mechanic: Present a compelling example or study before the main explanation, then promise to return later for methodological detail and qualifications.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the subject benefits from an emotionally or practically salient entry point before technical exposition.
mechanics.avoid: Do not let the opening example function as proof of a broad conclusion before its limitations are explained.

mechanics.mechanic: Identify a familiar shorthand, replace it with a more precise conceptual model, and signal that the model will organize the rest of the discussion.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when public language compresses several distinct processes into one misleading idea.
mechanics.avoid: Do not merely reject the shorthand; provide a usable replacement and explain why the distinction matters.

mechanics.mechanic: Introduce the central variable, then distinguish its baseline from temporary deviations, followed by separate dimensions such as location, scale, timing, or pathway.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for biological, technical, or systems topics in which one mechanism operates across multiple levels.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce specialized dimensions without first stating how each one connects to the main model.

mechanics.function: Translate technical structure into intuitive analogies
mechanics.mechanic: Pair unfamiliar terminology with a simple spatial, social, or process-based analogy, then return to the formal term so the analogy supports rather than replaces accuracy.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when explaining anatomy, circuitry, hierarchies, or abstract causal relationships to a mixed-knowledge audience.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid analogies that imply stronger one-to-one correspondence than the underlying mechanism supports.

mechanics.mechanic: Repeat a small set of paired distinctions throughout the explanation, applying each pair to new examples and progressively adding detail.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the audience must retain several related categories or compare mechanisms across cases.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce too many competing taxonomies; keep the recurring contrasts stable.

mechanics.mechanic: Separate general patterns from individual variation, distinguish animal or laboratory evidence from human experience, and identify when an example is illustrative rather than definitive.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever evidence varies by person, context, measurement method, or research design.
mechanics.avoid: Do not bury essential limitations after presenting precise-sounding numbers or universal conclusions.

mechanics.mechanic: Acknowledge an apparent exception, explain which part of the model it challenges, and refine the model by adding a moderating factor such as context, prior state, or subjective interpretation.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a broad rule risks sounding deterministic or when real-world outcomes differ across people.
mechanics.avoid: Do not dismiss counterexamples as irrelevant; show how they improve the explanatory framework.

mechanics.function: Close sections with a practical bridge
mechanics.mechanic: After explaining a mechanism, summarize the few elements the audience should retain and connect them to a decision, behavior, or future section.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at transitions from theory to application and at the end of dense technical passages.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce advice that depends on mechanisms or evidence that have not yet been established.
